newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot propane weakens, eyes on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada spot propane weakens, eyes on U.S..

text.p: Canada spot propane prices were brought down this week by falling U.S. values but found support in Canadian inventory data showing good builds, traders said on Thursday.
Traders said, however, they expect prices could drop further next week if values in the U.S. continue their free fall.
"If the U.S. keeps trading lower we are going to see a reduction," said one Eastern Canadian trader.
"Propane looks pretty good but it is so low in the states, it's just a drop in the bucket, she added.
In the Canadian goverment's inventory report released Thursday, total Canadian propane stocks rose 13.9 percent in the month of September and are currently 4.47 percent higher this year than last.
U.S. stocks, however, are at their lowest levels since 1970.
In Eastern Canada, propane grew 21.7 percent for the month, pegging levels 4.54 percent higher than this time last year.
On Thursday, spot prices in the hub traded about a quarter cent lower than last week at 54.00/54.25 cents.
In the Western hub of Edmonton, propane stocks rose 23.5 percent, putting it 16.2 percent higher this time last year.
Spot prices were assessed one cent lower at 44.50/45.50 cents.
The butanes, however, remained tight in both hubs, with normal rising a mere 4.14 percent and 24.8 percent below last year.
